posts.headline: North American Scrabble Championship comes to Cedar Rapids

platforms.name: X
platforms.why: one number and one quote, link preview does the work

platforms.name: Facebook
platforms.why: needs a sentence of setup, and a hotel ballroom in Iowa is a hometown story

posts.blurb: Three hundred competitive Scrabble players filled a Cedar Rapids hotel ballroom for the North American championship, where the top boards run on nine- and eleven-letter words.
posts.why: A national title decided in a room full of strangers who all showed up for the same board — the tournament end of our own genre.

posts.headline: Land of 10K Ryans: People named Ryan take over Mall of America for world record attempt

platforms.name: X
platforms.why: the premise is the whole post, link preview carries it

platforms.name: Instagram
platforms.why: a rollercoaster loaded entirely with Ryans stands on the image alone — feed post

posts.blurb: More than a thousand people legally named Ryan flew to the Mall of America from as far as Alaska and Hawaii to ride the Ryan-coaster together. Then they drove to Ryan, Iowa, for the key to the city.
posts.why: A thousand strangers organizing a weekend around one shared arbitrary rule — that is a game, and they built it themselves.

posts.headline: For Three Hours Every Day, Open Ocean Transforms Into Australia's 'Ghost' Reef

platforms.name: Instagram
platforms.why: photographs of a reef surfacing out of open water carry it — feed post

platforms.name: Facebook
platforms.why: first-person piece that earns the click once you explain the tide

posts.blurb: Montgomery Reef sits 1,200 miles from the nearest Australian city and is invisible most of the day. For about three hours the tide drops and 100,000 acres of coral rises out of the Indian Ocean.
posts.why: A place that only exists if you show up at the right hour — the purest version of playing where you are standing.

posts.headline: Charlene DeLoach previews top games ahead of Gen Con in Indianapolis

platforms.name: X
platforms.why: games-culture news where the link is the payload

posts.blurb: Gen Con opens in Indianapolis on July 30 and hundreds of games debut on the floor. One of them, a card game called Rush of Icor, is running a tournament with a six-figure prize pool.
posts.why: The biggest week of the year for tabletop, and the crowd walking that floor is exactly our crowd.

posts.headline: A centuries-old festival in Japan brings Shinto traditions and towering floats to the streets

platforms.name: Instagram
platforms.why: thirteen AP frames of floats and purification rites need no caption — feed post

platforms.name: Facebook
platforms.why: the thousand-year plague origin is the hook, and it takes a sentence

posts.blurb: Kyoto's Gion Matsuri began more than a thousand years ago as a ritual to ward off plague. It still takes the whole of July, with towering floats hauled through the streets by hand.
posts.why: A city that turns itself into the event for a month, which is the scale every route we build is reaching for.
